quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best riding formation?
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding on curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress for bad weather, limit riding to about six hours per day, and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also play a role.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction to be done safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle carrying a passenger sits differently because of the extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you easily.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or pavement seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. If you inch across slowly, the tracks can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. Besides their safety benefits, they protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not necessary when wearing a full-face helmet.
Prevents you from hearing necessary road noises, such as horns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is encouraged.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Earplugs provide hearing protection while still letting you hear car horns and emergency sirens.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and press harder on the brakes.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Your tire grip is needed to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When riding in a group, who should set the speed?

options.text: The rider behind the lead rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The sweep rider
questions.explanation: The sweep rider is the last rider in the group and should set the speed. This keeps the group together and prevents riders from separating.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to turn the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try turning the throttle back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn. To turn left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To turn right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from driving drunk, arrange other transportation, involve friends to help stop them, and keep them from leaving before they are sober. Do not suggest they drive on different roads.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Keep a larger distance from other vehicles.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase your distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, which formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for normal group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When wet, the center of a lane is dangerous. When it rains, avoid the center by riding in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet.
Yes, in addition to a helmet.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Hearing protection helps guard against this damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When may you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. You need more distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or in heavy traffic where another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: For maximum braking power, what should the rider do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Not lock either wheel.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line braking, apply both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel.
